keywords.def: pot of stew into which new ingredients are regularly added so that the food is kept going and can be eaten over a long time
cooking at a temperature slightly below boiling so that the food bubbles gently
from the beginning, without the help of anything that has already been made
difficult to do; taking a lot of time and effort

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的《6 Minute English》。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Beth. Most people have eaten some unusual food at least once in their life.
sentences.zh: 我是Phil。我是Beth。大多数人一生中至少吃过一些不寻常的食物。

sentences.en: What's the most unusual thing you've ever eaten, Beth?
sentences.zh: Beth，你吃过的最不寻常的东西是什么？

sentences.en: Oh, I ate camel in Australia, and I really didn't like it, to be honest.
sentences.zh: 哦，我在澳大利亚吃过骆驼肉，说实话，我真的不喜欢。

sentences.en: What about you? I ate caiman in Northern Argentina, and it was delicious!
sentences.zh: 你呢？我在阿根廷北部吃过凯门鳄，味道好极了！

sentences.en: Oh, OK. Good! Well, in this programme we'll be discussing some very unusual food known as 'forever food' – dishes, like stews and soups, which can be kept going day after day, year after year.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。太好了！在这期节目中，我们将讨论一些非常不寻常的食物，被称为“永久食物”——比如炖菜和汤这样的菜肴，可以日复一日、年复一年地一直做下去。

sentences.en: We'll also be learning some useful new vocabulary, all of which you can download, along with a worksheet for this programme, at our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们还将学习一些实用的新词汇，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上下载这些词汇以及本节目的练习页。

sentences.en: But let's get back to forever food, and a Bangkok restaurant called, Wattana Panich, that's famous for a soup which has been cooking for over 50 years!
sentences.zh: 但让我们回到“永久食物”上来，曼谷有一家名为 Wattana Panich 的餐馆，以一锅已经煮了50多年的汤而闻名！

sentences.en: Here's radio listener, David Shirley, who called BBC World Service programme, The Food Chain, after tasting the soup himself: I had never heard of a perpetual stew before, but the first time I'd ever heard about it was when I was in Bangkok.
sentences.zh: 这位是电台听众大卫·希尔利（David Shirley），他在自己品尝了这道汤后，给BBC世界服务部的节目《The Food Chain》打去了电话：我以前从未听说过永生炖菜，但第一次听说是在曼谷。

sentences.en: I found a stew that had been simmering for fifty years.
sentences.zh: 我发现了一锅已经慢炖了五十年的炖菜。

sentences.en: David tasted perpetual stew, a pot into which ingredients are placed and cooked continuously.
sentences.zh: 大卫品尝了永生炖菜，这是一个不断放入食材并持续烹饪的锅。

sentences.en: The pot is never completely emptied. Instead, new ingredients and water are added when necessary and left simmering – cooking at a temperature just below boiling so that the food bubbles gently.
sentences.zh: 锅里的东西从来没有完全清空过。相反，必要时会加入新的食材和水，并保持慢炖——在略低于沸点的温度下烹饪，让食物轻轻冒泡。

sentences.en: A 50-year-old soup might not be to everyone's taste, but forever foods are surprisingly common.
sentences.zh: 一锅50年的汤可能不合所有人的胃口，但“永久食物”却出奇地普遍。

sentences.en: And, Phil, I have a question for you about Wattana Panich' s 50-year-old soup.
sentences.zh: 而且，Phil，我有一个关于 Wattana Panich 50年老汤的问题要问你。

sentences.en: What do you think is the main ingredient?
sentences.zh: 你认为主要的食材是什么？

sentences.en: Is it: a) beef? b) chicken? or, c) vegetables?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 牛肉？ b) 鸡肉？ 还是 c) 蔬菜？

sentences.en: Oh, I think vegetables. I think that's probably safer.
sentences.zh: 哦，我认为是蔬菜。我觉得这样可能更安全。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out the correct answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。嗯，我们会在节目后半段揭晓正确答案。

sentences.en: It's not just Bangkok where people cook forever foods.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是曼谷有人在做“永久食物”。

sentences.en: Fuchsia Dunlop is a writer and cook specialising in Chinese food.
sentences.zh: 扶霞·邓洛普（Fuchsia Dunlop）是一位专门研究中国美食的作家和厨师。

sentences.en: Here, she tells BBC World Service programme, 'The Food Chain', about a Chinese stew that is rumoured to be 100 years old: In China they sometimes, you know, professionals talk about having a bǎinián laolu which means, like, a 100-year-old-broth.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她向BBC世界服务部的节目《The Food Chain》讲述了一道据传有100年历史的中式炖菜：在中国，有时候专业人士会谈论所谓的“百年老卤”，意思是像100年历史的高汤。

sentences.en: So, I don't know if this is strictly true, but theoretically as long as you have a good practice of hygiene - which is to say that you always skim it, and boil it every day, and also replenish it as needed with more water, more salt, more spices, and you know, you keep tasting - then it just gets richer and richer.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道这是否严格意义上的真实，但理论上，只要你保持良好的卫生习惯——也就是说你总是撇去浮沫，每天煮沸，并根据需要补充更多的水、更多的盐、更多的香料，你知道的，不断品尝——那么它就会变得越来越浓郁。

sentences.en: Cooks need to replenish a forever stew, to fill it up again with fresh ingredients before it's completely eaten.
sentences.zh: 厨师需要补充永久炖菜，在它被完全吃完之前，重新加入新鲜食材填满它。

sentences.en: By being regularly replenished, some dishes are rumoured to last 100 years.
sentences.zh: 通过定期补充，据传有些菜肴能持续100年。

sentences.en: Wow, that is a long time! Fuchsia doesn't know if it's strictly true, or completely true, that the same stew has really lasted 100 years, but she thinks it's possible in theory, as long as it's kept safe and hygienic through boiling.
sentences.zh: 哇，那真是太久了！扶霞不知道同一锅炖菜真的持续了100年是否完全属实，但她认为在理论上是可能的，只要通过煮沸保持安全和卫生。

sentences.en: Professor Martha Carlin is a historian with a special interest in medieval cookery.
sentences.zh: 玛莎·卡林教授（Professor Martha Carlin）是一位对中世纪烹饪有特殊兴趣的历史学家。

sentences.en: Here, she explains to BBC World Service programme, 'The Food Chain', why long-lasting foods could have been familiar to people in the Middle Ages: In theory, it would make sense to think that people who didn't have matches or fire starters, for whom starting a fire from scratch was quite a cumbersome process, would naturally want to keep a stew pot bubbling if they had the means to do that, and to avoid the labour of constantly restarting the fire, and also to make sure that they had a hot meal waiting at any time.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她向BBC世界服务部的节目《The Food Chain》解释了为什么中世纪的人们会对持久的食物习以为常：从理论上讲，人们没有火柴或生火工具，从头开始生火对他们来说是一个相当繁琐的过程，如果他们有条件的话，自然会想让炖锅一直咕嘟咕嘟冒泡，避免不断重新生火的劳累，并确保随时都有热腾腾的饭菜等着他们，这在逻辑上是讲得通的。

sentences.en: Having hot food bubbling away on the fire means there' is always something ready to eat, and avoids having to start a fire from scratch.
sentences.zh: 热腾腾的食物在火上咕嘟咕嘟作响，意味着随时都有东西可以吃，免去了从头生火的麻烦。

sentences.en: When you do something, like cook food or make a fire, from scratch, you do it from the beginning, without the help of anything that has already been made.
sentences.zh: 当你从头（from scratch）做某事，比如烹饪食物或生火时，你是从最初开始做，没有利用任何已经做好的东西。

sentences.en: Starting a fire is also cumbersome, an adjective meaning difficult to do, taking time and effort.
sentences.zh: 生火也是繁琐的（cumbersome），这个形容词的意思是难以做到，需要时间和精力。

sentences.en: But Professor Carlin says only rich families were able to afford enough wood to keep a fire going all day.
sentences.zh: 但卡林教授说，只有富裕的家庭才能负担得起足够的木柴来让火整天燃烧。

sentences.en: Anyway, all this talk of food has made me hungry, Beth, so what was the answer to your question?
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，说了这么多食物让我饿了，Beth，你问题的答案是什么？

sentences.en: Ah, I asked you what the main ingredient is in the Bangkok stew, and you said vegetables.
sentences.zh: 啊，我问你曼谷炖菜的主要成分是什么，你说是蔬菜。

sentences.en: And I'm afraid that's wrong. It was, in fact, beef.
sentences.zh: 恐怕你猜错了。事实上，它是牛肉。

sentences.en: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this programme about forever foods such as perpetual stew, a pot of stew into which new ingredients are regularly added, allowing the dish to be eaten over a long time.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回顾一下本节目中学习的关于“永久食物”的词汇，比如永生炖菜，这是一种定期添加新食材的炖菜锅，可以让这道菜在很长一段时间内被食用。

sentences.en: When food is simmering, it's cooking at a temperature slightly below boiling so that it bubbles gently.
sentences.zh: 当食物在慢炖（simmering）时，它在略低于沸点的温度下烹饪，以便轻轻冒泡。

sentences.en: The verb replenish means to fill something up again.
sentences.zh: 动词补充（replenish）的意思是再次把某物填满。

sentences.en: If something is not strictly true, it's not completely or entirely true.
sentences.zh: 如果某事不是严格意义上的真实（not strictly true），那它就不是完全或绝对真实。

sentences.en: When you do an activity such as cooking, from scratch, you do it from the beginning, without using anything that has already been made.
sentences.zh: 当你从头（from scratch）开展烹饪等活动时，你是从最初开始，不使用任何已经做好的东西。

sentences.en: And finally, if an activity is cumbersome, it's difficult to do and takes a lot of time and effort.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果一项活动是繁琐的（cumbersome），做起来就很困难，需要花费大量时间和精力。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. Remember to visit our website, bbclearningenglish.com, where you'll find a worksheet and a quiz related to this programme, and we'll see you again soon for more trending topics and useful vocabulary, here at 6 Minute English.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了。记得访问我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，在那里你会找到与本节目相关的练习页和测验，我们很快就会在《6 Minute English》再次见面，带来更多热门话题和实用词汇。

sentences.en: Goodbye for now! Bye!
sentences.zh: 先这样啦！再见！
